title: M/S Shah Concast Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Siddhartha Varma, J.; Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal, J.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed for want of prosecution; interim order vacated.
headnote: A consumer who had opted for a pre-payment meter challenged a 29 September 2012 additional-security demand as illegal under Section 47(5) of the Electricity Act, 2003, and attacked Clause 4.20(l) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as ultra vires that sub-section, also relying on the absence of Section 181(2)(v) regulations and on Section 174. On 10 December 2012 the Division Bench connected the writ with M/s Supreme Ceramics Limited (W.P. No. 51844 of 2009) and other similar petitions, and stayed the demand on an undertaking to furnish the security if the writ failed. On 3 July 2023, none appearing for the petitioner even in the revised call, the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution and the interim order vacated. The Section 47 / Clause 4.20(l) questions were not decided.
facts:
M/S Shah Concast Pvt. Ltd. challenged Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.'s demand of additional security in a bill dated 29 September 2012. It said it had opted for a pre-payment meter, so the demand under Section 47(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003 was illegal in view of Section 47(5); that Clause 4.20(l) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was ultra vires Section 47(5); that security regulations under Section 181(2)(v) of the Act had not been framed; and that Section 174 overrode inconsistent Code provisions.

Counsel for both sides treated the controversy as the same as in Civil Misc. Writ Petition No. 51844 of 2009 (M/s Supreme Ceramics Limited v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.) and connected petitions in which interim orders had been passed. On 10 December 2012 the Court connected this writ with those petitions, issued notice, and, without prejudice, restrained the respondents from demanding the additional security if the petitioner filed an undertaking to furnish it should the writ fail. After listings from November 2012, the petition was called in the revised list on 3 July 2023.

holding_units.topic: additional security / pre-payment meter; writ dismissed for want of prosecution
holding_units.holding: On 10 December 2012 the Court recorded the petitioner's case that additional security demanded under Section 47(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003 was illegal because it had opted for a pre-payment meter (Section 47(5)), that Clause 4.20(l) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was ultra vires Section 47(5), that security regulations under Section 181(2)(v) had not been framed, and that Section 174 overrode inconsistent provisions; the licensee did not dispute that the same controversy was pending in W.P. No. 51844 of 2009 and connected writs. The Court connected the petitions and, without prejudice, directed that the respondents not demand the additional security in the bill dated 29 September 2012 if the petitioner filed an undertaking to furnish it should the writ fail. On 3 July 2023, none appearing for the petitioner even in the revised call, the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution and the interim order vacated, without deciding those points.
holding_units.flag: Thin procedural disposal. Order-sheet 5.11.2012–3.7.2023 (adjournments, then the 10.12.2012 interim, then dismissal). The 2023 order has no numbered paragraphs. Coram is the disposing bench (Siddhartha Varma and Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal, JJ.); the 2012 orders were Satya Poot Mehrotra and Het Singh Yadav, JJ. Clause 4.20(l) and Sections 47(2)/(5), 174 and 181(2)(v) are as invoked; they were not construed.

principle_tags.application: After a 2012 without-prejudice stay of an additional-security demand under Section 47(2) / Clause 4.20(l) on a pre-payment-meter undertaking, the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution when none appeared even in the revised call, and the interim order was vacated, leaving the Section 47(5) and ultra vires points undecided.
